questions.question: What does an `async function` always return, regardless of what its `return` statement specifies?
options: The raw value from the return statement, with no wrapping
A Promise that resolves with the returned value
questions.explanation: Declaring a function async guarantees it returns a Promise; a plain `return value` becomes a Promise resolved with that value.

questions.question: What happens when you `await` a Promise that rejects, inside a try/catch block?
options: The rejection is thrown as an error at that point, which the surrounding catch block can handle
try/catch cannot catch Promise rejections at all
It causes an unhandled promise rejection regardless of the try/catch
questions.explanation: A rejected awaited Promise behaves like a thrown exception, so a normal try/catch around the await handles it.

questions.question: Why is `await fetchA(); await fetchB();` slower than `await Promise.all([fetchA(), fetchB()])` when A and B don't depend on each other?
options: There is no actual difference in timing
Sequential awaits make fetchB wait until fetchA fully completes before even starting, while Promise.all starts both immediately and waits for the slower one
Promise.all makes each request faster individually
await always runs twice as slow as Promise.all for any input
questions.explanation: Sequential awaits don't start the second request until the first resolves, adding their durations; starting both at once and awaiting together takes roughly the duration of the slower one.

questions.question: What does `await` actually pause when used inside an async function?
options: The entire JavaScript runtime, blocking all other code
Only the execution of that specific async function, while the rest of the program continues running via the event loop
Only the browser's rendering, not JavaScript execution
Nothing — await has no effect on execution order
questions.explanation: await suspends just the current async function's continuation until its Promise settles; it does not block the single JS thread from doing other work in the meantime.
